content: The content provided lists various experts, their affiliations, and their contributions to occupational health and safety, particularly in the context of manufactured nanomaterials (MNMs). Below is a professional interpretation of the information: 1. Contributors and Affiliations: Mahmoud Ghazi-Khansari is affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences in Iran. Mary Gulumian works in the Toxicology and Biochemistry Department at the National Institute for Occupational Health (NIOH) in Johannesburg, South Africa. Evelyn Kortum is part of the World Health Organization (WHO), focusing on public health, environmental, and social determinants of health in Geneva, Switzerland. Naroo Lee is associated with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) in Ulsan, Republic of Korea. Yair Ray Lifshitz is from the Research Center for Ergonomics, Industrial Engineering, and Management at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology in Haifa, Israel. Jaroslav Mraz is part of the National Institute of Public Health, Center of Occupational Health in Prague, Czech Republic. Vladimir Murashov is affiliated with the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) in Washington, DC, USA. Toshihiko Myojo works at the Institute of Industrial Ecological Sciences, University of Occupational and Environmental Health (UOEH) in Iseigaoka, Japan. Rolf Packroff is with the Federal Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (BAuA) in Dortmund, Germany. Aida Ponce del Castillo is part of the European Trade Union Institute in Brussels, Belgium. Darius D. Sivin is associated with the International Union, UAW, Health & Safety Department in Washington, DC, USA. Pieter van Broekhuizen is from IVAM, University of Amsterdam (UvA) in the Netherlands. Maria de Fatima Torres F. Viegas is affiliated with Fundacentro, Ministry of Labour and Social Security in São Paulo, Brazil. William Waissmann works at the Sergio Arouca National School of Public Health, Fundação Oswaldo Cruz in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Yuxin Zheng is part of the National Institute of Occupational Health, China Center for Disease Control and Prevention in Beijing, China. Arline Sydnéia Abel Arcuri is associated with Fundacentro, Ministry of Labour in São Paulo, Brazil. Bill Kojola is part of the American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations (AFL-CIO) in Washington, DC, USA. Claude Ostiguy works at the Institut de Recherche Robert-Sauvé en Santé et en Sécurité du Travail in Québec, Canada. Judy Sng is affiliated with the National University of Singapore. Nathalie Thieriet is part of the French Agency for Food, Environmental, and Occupational Health and Safety (ANSES) in Paris, France. Jeong-Sun Yang is associated with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) in Ulsan, Republic of Korea. 2. Systematic Review Teams: Experts such as Skaug V., Zienolddiny S., and Mohr B. contributed to assessing risks of manufactured nanomaterials (MNMs). They are affiliated with INAIL, the Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work in Rome, Italy. Mihalache R., Verbeek J., Graczyk H., Murashov V., and van Broekhuizen P. Eastlake A., Zumwalde R., and Geraci C. focused on control banding techniques, representing the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) in Cincinnati, OH, USA. Myojo T. and Nagata T. developed specific risk mitigation techniques at the University of Occupational and Environmental Health in Kitakyushu, Japan. Gulumian M., Verbeek J., Andraos C., Sanabria N., and de Jager P. Von Mering Y. and Schumacher C. Andrade L.R.B. emphasized the involvement of workers and their representatives in addressing the impacts of nanotechnology on worker health and the environment, representing Fundacentro in São Paulo, Brazil. 3.
